## Purpose

The crate root of `mustard-cli` is a deliberately small module layer of four files: `lib.rs` (the library face the Tauri dashboard links against), `main.rs` (the binary face), `cli.rs` (`clap` parsing plus the dispatch table), and `fs_ops.rs` (filesystem and JSON primitives shared by the subcommands). `lib.rs` is the only place crate-wide lints are declared (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and the test-only `clippy::unwrap_used` / `clippy::expect_used` exemption), and it is the single registry of `pub mod` entries; `main.rs` stays a thin shell that maps `Result` onto `ExitCode` and prints `[mustard] error: {err:#}`, so all real logic remains reusable from the library. Every module opens with a `//!` block that states its role, its callers, and — when relevant — what was retired and why, so the file explains itself before the first `use`. Fallible work returns `anyhow::Result<T>` and attaches `.with_context(|| format!("…{}", path.display()))` naming the path or operation; reads that a caller should not have to triage collapse to an empty value instead (`read_json_object`). Tests are not a separate tree: each file ends with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` driving real temp directories via `tempfile::tempdir`.

## Convention

- Folder: `apps/cli/src/` (crate root, non-recursive) — one level down, `commands/` holds one module per subcommand and follows its own mold.
- Extension: `.rs`, one snake_case file per module, no `mod.rs` at the crate root.
- File count: 4 (`lib.rs`, `main.rs`, `cli.rs`, `fs_ops.rs`).

## How to apply

A new crate-root module is a snake_case `.rs` file placed directly under `apps/cli/src/`, registered with `pub mod <name>;` in `lib.rs` beside the existing entries and given a matching bullet in the `lib.rs` `//!` module list, so the two never drift. Open the file with a `//!` block naming the module's job and its consumers, then `use std::…`, then external crates (`anyhow::{Context, Result}`, `serde_json`, `mustard_core::io::fs as mfs`), then `crate::…` — one group per block, blank line between. Public functions take borrowed paths (`&Path`) and return `anyhow::Result<T>`; wrap every I/O call in `.with_context(|| format!(…))` that names the affected path. Writes go through `mfs::write_atomic` with a trailing newline; JSON reads go through `fs_ops::read_json_object` and merge with `entry().or_insert_with(|| json!(…))` so user keys are never clobbered. Never introduce `unwrap`/`expect` outside `#[cfg(test)]`, never add logic to `main.rs`, and keep `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of the same file with `use super::*;` and a small local `write` helper when fixtures need one.

Adding a subcommand touches `cli.rs` in exactly three places: a doc-commented variant in the private `enum Commands` (with `#[arg]` attributes and `#[command(name = "…")]` when the CLI verb is kebab-case), a match arm in `dispatch` that constructs the command's options struct inline, and a `use crate::commands::<verb>::{self, <Verb>Options};` import. `run()` stays a one-liner over `dispatch(Cli::parse())` so tests can drive `dispatch` with `Cli::try_parse_from([...])` without a real `argv`.

## Examples

- Ref: `apps/cli/src/lib.rs` — crate lints, the `pub mod` registry, the single `pub use` re-export, and `VERSION` sourced from `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`.
- Ref: `apps/cli/src/cli.rs` — `Cli`/`Commands` derive types, `run()` → `dispatch()` split, and parser tests using `try_parse_from`.
- Ref: `apps/cli/src/fs_ops.rs` — shared primitives with `.with_context` on every I/O call, the fail-open `read_json_object`, and in-file `tempdir` tests.
